 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.328/ 2023 dated 27.4.2023 registered at Police Station Aarakshi Kendra Kotwali, District Tikamgarh for the offence under Sections 406, 409, 420, 467, 468 of IPC.

Applicant apprehending his arrest in the case has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
2.

As per the prosecution story, one complaint for commission of aforesaid offences was filed by one Vishnu Sharma against the present applicant before CJM, Tikamgarh alleging that applicant is working as daily wages employee and is also receiving honorarium from the government.
It was further alleged that he was not eligible for appointing as Pujari in the temple but concealing facts, he is working as Pujari of Jagdamba Badi Devi temple, Tikamgarh.
Earlier his father too has worked as Pujari of the temple.
He was also a Constable in police department.

sentences.text: He along with his family is residing in the temple premises and is doing some acts which are prohibited in the temple.
As such he is misusing his position and also creating problems to public at large.
Learned Magistrate forwarded complaint to police and directed to proceed under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. and directed for further investigation.
FIR was registered and the matter is still under investigation.
No charge sheet has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He is serving as Pujari in temple.
Temple is not a government temple though Collector is shown to be Manager of the temple and the land attached therewith.
It is further submitted that temple is a private temple and in this regard a civil suit is pending before the Civil Judge, Tikamgarh for determinating right of the applicant and government.
There is no specific and clear allegation against him as to how and in what capacity he embezzled the temple money.
Omnibus allegations have been made.
Such allegations hold no water.
Trial of the case will take considerable time as charge sheet has not been filed.
Therefore, it has been prayed that applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
4 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
5. I have gone through the material on record.

It is undisputed that civil suit is pending between the parties before the Civil Court for determination of right and to determine whether the temple is property of government or it is a private temple.
Undoubtedly, applicant is pujari of the temple.
At this stage it cannot be said that discharge of duties of pujari by the applicant are in any way falls in purview of offence under Section 409 of IPC.
Same has to be determined by the trial Court on the basis of evidence of the parties before it.

Considering all the facts and circumstances but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which custodial interrogation of the applicant is not warranted.
6. Consequently, this first anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicants stands allowed.

7. It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant - Shiv Kumar Nayak be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.
